utterances.text: They were coming from the "white house."

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how loud was this noise and screams and moans that you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was more or less in the middle of the pista. I was always near the wall. And those screams were so loud that we heard them well. And after all, that's not so close, but yet we could hear those screams and moans.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I have marked an exhibit 3/83. It is a photograph of the portion of the restaurant/administration building that faces onto the pista and toward the hangar. And I would ask that copies be distributed, the Defence should have copies already, and that the witness be provided the exhibit to look at the exhibit. I would also ask that the witness be given a pen and that this photograph be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you would look at this photograph and if you would mark with an "X" where you first saw this person who was calling out these names. Where you first saw him, if you would mark that with an "X".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, I would ask that you mark with an "X1" where this person was when you last saw him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, I would ask that you mark with a "KV" where Kvocka was when you first saw him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And I would ask that you mark with a "KV1" where Kvocka was when you last saw him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, as we look at this exhibit which you have marked, at one point you have "KV" and "X1" very close to each other. As you observed this incident, Kvocka and the man calling out the names, did you ever see them standing this close to each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see them speak to each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them speak to each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that exhibit could be removed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you have also testified about the shift leader known to you as Krle and you indicated that there was an incident that you observed that involved Krle. At this point I would like for you to tell the Court about this incident which involved Krle, and again I would like you to speak very slowly and very clearly and begin with what first captured your attention and then tell the Court what you observed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time we were sitting on the pista, as usual, and a man got up and started walking up and down on the pista. And Krle shouted, "Sit down. Go back to your place," but the man didn't do what he was told. He continued walking up and down. Krle shouted, "Go back," so it was normal that we were looking in that direction. Krle took him and led him in the direction of the "white house." After a short time Krle came back because they were about to have a change of shift. After a short time I heard a burst of fire, and the normal reaction was to look in the direction of the fire. And we looked towards the "white house." That man jumped up, of fear or what, and then again I hear the voice say, "Stop," and when I looked around who the voice belonged to, it was Krle's. He was saying, "Stop," and he -- it was Krle, and he went towards him and fired. I don't know the man's name. He fell on the grass. And we were ordered to lie face down, and after that I don't know what happened. That is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, when the man was led toward the "white house," and then the next thing that caught your attention was that you heard a burst of fire coming from the "white house"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the direction of the "white house," yes, but it was like the shattering of glass. And I turned around and saw Krle coming towards us along the grass, towards the pista.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: So when you heard the shattering of glass, where did you look?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that direction where the noise had come from, and it was from the "white house" and that is where I turned to look.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you looked toward the "white house," what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a short while I saw this man walking towards us along the grass. He seemed to be not all there, out of fear or what. And then Krle was saying, "Stop. Wait." The man didn't. Krle went up to him and fired. That was the first time I saw a man killed, and that is something that has stuck in my mind all this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, this man that you saw walking toward you along the grass, was this the same man that you had seen taken toward the "white house" earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same man. He must have sort of been a bit crazy. His nerves had given in or something.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you heard someone calling out "Stop," where did you look?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the direction of the restaurant, because that is where the voice came from. Before that he had been taken away. So I saw Krle shouting "Stop" and going towards this man, this man didn't stop, and Krle opened fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, when you saw Krle shouting "Stop," going toward the man and then firing, did you see any guards in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were guards around him, but I saw that Krle had a gun. There were some guards around him. I can't remember whether anyone was following him. But at that moment I saw Krle, and they were expecting a change of shift and they were standing there. And I saw Krle approach this man and fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall how long you had been in the camp when this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The incident -- the incident, as far as I can recollect, occurred, I think, a month after I arrived and more. I think Kvocka had been replaced by Meakic. I think Kvocka had already left by then.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, after you left Omarska camp, after that time, did you ever see the man you knew as Krkan either in person or on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did see Krkan in a television programme.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what that television programme was about, why Krkan was on that programme?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was something but in a language I didn't understand. I just recognised the camp, or the part of the camp that was being shown. But what exactly the programme was about, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall being interviewed in 1998 by an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time do you recall being shown three different sets of photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: For each of those sets of photographs, do you recall having a procedure read to you in a language you understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall signing the written notice of those procedures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember signing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall that as regards one set of photographs, you told the investigator that you did not recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: As to the other two sets of photographs, do you recall telling the investigator that you did recognise someone on each of those sets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that I recognised two persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who were the persons that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On one set I recognised Kvocka and in the other set I recognised Krle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: This Kvocka that you recognised on this set, was this the Kvocka who introduced himself and said he was responsible for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is this the same Kvocka who was present when you testified you heard Kiki and the others called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same person. Kvocka, I saw him then as he was leaving, when Kiki was being called out.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: As to Krle, was this the Krle you knew in the camp to be one of the shift commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is Krle that I knew as a shift commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was it this same Krle you have just testified you saw shout "Stop" and shoot his weapon at a detainee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same person that I recognised, who said "Stop" and who shot at the prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution would mark as an exhibit the exhibit next in line, which is 3/84, 3/84A, 3/84B, 3/84C, and 3/84D. The Defence has previously been provided with copies of this, and I have provided the Registry with copies for Your Honours. And if I could have assistance and if the Defence could be shown the photo board so that they know which I'm dealing with. Not the witness but the Defence counsel. Now, if the witness could be provided with 84A.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, would you look at that and tell me if you recognise your signature on that page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. That is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown 84D, "D," "D" as in Delta, and if that could be put on the ELMO, please. And if you could please ensure that all of those photos are visible on the ELMO. The other way.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you would please point to the person you recognise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know this individual to be Kvocka [indicates], number 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that could be retrieved, please. Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution would mark as an exhibit 3/85A, 3/85B, 3/85C, 3/85D, and 3/85D1. Again, copies have been provided. If the Defence could be show that first, please. And if the witness could please be shown "A".

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Does your signature appear on that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. That is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown D and D1, please. And then if those could be put on the overhead, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please point to the person you recognised on that photo array.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised this man under number 4 [indicates]. He was shift leader Krle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you look on the back of those photographs, please. Does your signature appear on the back of those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does appear on the back, my signature, on these photographs. And under number 4, I recognised the person.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If D of 84 could also be provided to the witness again. Is that the original?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you look and see if your signature appears on the back of that as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it appears on the back, my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that could be retrieved, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, when you were taken from Omarska camp, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken from Omarska to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, you have testified to the Judges about the beatings and the conditions, as far as you were concerned, in Omarska camp. When you left Omarska camp, what was your physical condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had lost about 20 kilos, between 15 and 20 kilograms. I don't know exactly. My state of health was terrible; I was ill. And that's how I arrived in Trnopolje, alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you went to Omarska camp, how much did you weigh?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before I was 70, 72 kilograms. My weight was about 70 kilograms.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: And when you left Omarska camp, if you know, how much did you weigh?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Afterwards, when I came home from Trnopolje, I weighed 55, 54 kilograms. I now have 59 kilos, and I find it difficult to regain my former weight, the weight that I had before I went to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we need to conclude this in private session, if we could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We shall be going into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: 2.25 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of May, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
